claims.statement: Joe Goss challenged Tom Allen for the championship for a stake of $2,500 a side (printed as $2.500).
claims.excerpt: Joe issued a challenge to Tom to contend for the honors of the position and a stake of $2.500 a side

claims.statement: Allen promptly accepted Goss's challenge and a match was speedily made.
claims.excerpt: he promptly accepted and a match was speedily made

claims.statement: Before the Goss fight Allen had gained fame and money in America and was generally regarded as the rightful champion.
claims.excerpt: who had gained fame and made money during his sojourn in the States, and was generally regarded as the rightful possessor of the championship title

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Joe Goss on 7 September 1876 on Kentucky soil, the ring first pitched in Kenton County.
claims.excerpt: They fought September 7, 1876, on Kentucky soil, the ring being first pitched in Kenton County

claims.statement: The Allen-Goss fight lasted twenty-one rounds and forty-eight minutes.
claims.excerpt: fought twenty-one rounds in all. in forty-eignt minutes

claims.statement: Goss was given the decision on account of a foul, so Allen lost the fight.
claims.excerpt: a decision was given in Goss’ favor. on account of a foul

claims.statement: The Kenton County grand jury indicted the principals of the Goss fight, including Allen.
claims.excerpt: Indictments were fonnd by the Grand Jury of Kenton County

claims.statement: Allen jumped his $3,000 bail (printed as $3,090) and crossed into Canada.
claims.excerpt: Allen jumping his bail, $3,090, and cros“ing into Canada

claims.statement: From Canada Allen went by steamer to England.
claims.excerpt: and cros“ing into Canada, whence he proceeded by steamerto England

fights.place: Kentucky soil; ring first pitched in Kenton County, then moved to Boone County
fights.excerpt: They fought September 7, 1876, on Kentucky soil, the ring being first pitched in Kenton County
fights.notes: Decided for Goss on a foul. The article says Allen was in much the better condition, Goss having trained too fine and gone stale.

notes: Article is mainly about Joe Goss; only the Allen facts are kept. OCR 1576 for 1876.
